sentence: This project studies how parts of the kisspeptin system in monkeys and man affect reproductive development and tests receptor antagonists as a possible treatment.
This project studies how close contact between cell types in adipose tissue controls the growth and remodeling of fat tissue.
This project studies how a type of receptor shapes brain development and synaptic transmission in seizure disorders.
This project studies how single cells read and produce changing signals of a signaling protein, using live imaging and CRISPR screening.
This project tests whether a receptor is a target for treating Alzheimer's disease using two existing drugs.
This project tries to find out how mutations in a transporter gene cause anemia and what treatments might help.
This project builds a metabolomics platform that finds metabolites and biomarkers to help explain disease mechanisms.
This project builds contrast agents that let shortwave infrared light show biological processes through tissue in mammals.
This project builds a paper-based self test that directly detects the genetic material of HIV.
This project studies how losing acetylcholine release or signaling in mouse models of Lewy Body Dementia leads to cortical dysfunction and cognitive decline.
This project supplies aging mice, rats, mole-rats and marmosets, and tests ways to promote healthy aging across their lifespan.
This project studies how a Parkinson's disease gene changes the spread of protein aggregates between cells in fruit fly and mouse models.
This project designs mRNA lipid nanoparticle vaccines against a retrovirus that causes leukemia and studies the immune response they trigger.
This project follows children with chronic kidney disease into adulthood to find out how childhood risk factors affect later health.
This project studies what happens to the pieces of RNA that form when cellular stress causes cleavage, and how they relate to human disease.
This project analyzes genome-wide gene expression and chromatin data from rodent and human brain in models of addiction.
This project builds wound treatments from glycosaminoglycan biopolymers that release nitric oxide to kill pathogens and calm inflammation in chronic wounds.
This project studies how mitochondrial DNA is packaged and used to make genes work, and how that changes with metabolism and stress.
This project studies whether targeting antigens on malignant plasma cells can treat multiple myeloma that returns after earlier therapy.
This project tests stimulating brainstem neurons that project down the spinal cord to help control blood pressure after spinal cord injury.
